content: The piano suits intimate, tender and grieving scenes. It's warm in the middle register and fragile in the high one.
A solo cello in its low register carries longing, grief and intimacy. Start with long bows and little vibrato, then let it bloom on the phrase peak.
The sordino violins suit melancholic scenes, because they sound soft, rich and distant.
French horns suit heroic adventure themes, and they sound epic played legato in a crescendo.
The church organ suits the murder in a noir film, where it marks the fatality.
For epic or action scenes in D minor, the progression i-VI-III-VII (Dm Bb F C) keeps moving and never fully resolves.
For melancholy in D minor, play i-VI-III-VII (Dm Bb F C) slowly. It's the same progression as the epic one, only softer and rubato.
For a noir funeral march in G minor at 68 bpm in 4/4, the progression iv-V-i-V (Cm D Gm D) keeps circling around the same dark chord.
A character theme needs a short motif the audience can hum. Vary it later: slower for grief, brighter for the triumphant return.
In an action chase at 124 bpm in 4/4, 1/16 triplets in percussion and staccato strings make a driving rhythm, loud and steady from the first bar.
In a noir funeral march at 68 bpm in 4/4, slow triplets in percussion and harp make a heavy rhythm that keeps coming.
For an action chase, orchestrate percussion and staccato strings together in 1/16 triplets, with ominous lows on 1/4 root notes underneath.
To raise the tension in an action chase, orchestrate high staccato strings in 1/8 notes above the ominous lows.
For a lonely, melancholic scene, orchestrate a solo cello melody over simple piano chords that change on each bar.
To wrap a melancholic moment in a richer sound, orchestrate sordino violins playing rich chords above the solo cello.
For a noir murder, orchestrate a slow funeral march with piano on root notes, and percussion and harp marking the triplets.
To make a noir scene ominous, orchestrate a church organ doubling the harp, while the piano adds phrases in octaves.
Arrange an action chase cue as three sections that build: first percussion, staccato strings and ominous lows, then add high strings, and save the legato French horns for the final section.
Arrange a melancholic drama cue as three sections that grow: solo cello and piano, then the cello rising in intensity, and finally sordino violins joining with rich chords.
Arrange a noir cue in sections that build: first the slow march, then a solo cello, and save the church organ for the final section.
For nostalgia, I use vinyl crackle as a sound effect under the music.
John Williams fanfares rely on quartal leaps and dotted rhythms, so the energy comes from the rhythm more than the harmony.
A gothic noir in the style of Bernard Herrmann leans on low piano octaves and dark organ chords.
Spot the picture before writing a note. Mark every hit point and build the tempo map, then compose to the cuts.
